content.title: Park and Recreation Month
content.summary: Seth Schafer won the Park and Recreation Month Photo Contest with his stunning sunrise photo at Lake Arbor, as voted by the community. The contest also recognized three finalists: Patric Stanton, Amanda Burck, and Rick Enochs, each showcasing their own impressive park images.
content.body:
## Arvada Parks Photo Contest Winner

A huge thank you to everyone who participated and voted in the Park and Recreation Month Photo Contest!

**The winner, as voted on by the community, is Seth Schafer and his photo of a beautiful sunrise at Lake Arbor. Congratulations Seth!**

### Arvada Parks Photo Contest Winner: Seth Schafer, Lake Arbor

![fiery looking sunset at a lake with ducks in the lake ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=6211 "fiery looking sunset at a lake with ducks in the lake ")

Congratulations to our three other finalists: Patric Stanton, Amanda Burck and Rick Enochs!

Each July the City of Arvada and the Apex Park and Recreation District celebrate national Park and Recreation Month in Arvada. Park and Recreation Month is an opportunity to celebrate how Arvada is stronger, more vibrant and more resilient through the power of parks and recreation.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6068)

Park and Recreation Month is also an opportunity to recognize and celebrate the hundreds of park and recreational professionals and volunteers who maintain our parks, trails and recreation facilities to ensure they are safe, beautiful and enjoyable for everyone.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6066)

## 2025 Arvada Park and Recreation Month Photo Contest

Celebrate Park and Recreation Month in Arvada this July by participating in the Park and Recreation Month Photo contest!

We invite you to share your photos of your favorite parks, trails and open space areas in Arvada. With more than 100 park sites and 150 miles of trails, there's plenty of inspiration!

### How to participate

- **Submit your Park and Recreation Month photos by emailing them to [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#6a0f040d0b0d0f2a0b181c0b0e0b4405180d)**
- Send no more than 3 photos
- When submitting your photo(s), include your name and the location of where the photo was taken
- Please do not submit photos with watermarks, logos, dates or any other text on them
- Photos do not have to be taken this month (July 2025)
- Submit your photos between Tuesday, July 1 and Sunday, July 20

### How the contest works

- Once the submission period closes on midnight, Sunday July 20, City staff will select up to 10 finalists
- The community will then have the opportunity to vote on the winning photos from Wednesday, July 23 to Tuesday, July 29
- The winning photo will be announced on Thursday, July 31
- Selected photos will be featured on the City's social media platforms and other public communication channels
- Prizes will be given to all finalists; prizes include:
  - Punch pass to Apex Park and Recreation District
  - Olde Town gift card
  - 18-hole round of golf for two people at Lake Arbor Golf Course
  - City of Arvada swag bags

### Photo contest guidelines

**Participants in the contest agree to the following release:**

By submitting a photo to Arvada for the Park and Recreation Month Photo Contest, you grant the City of Arvada the right to use the submitted image in conjunction with your name for any informational presentation, print collateral and promotions, social media and websites, and informational/educational media without any form of compensation or royalties. You further guarantee you have adequate rights in the photo to grant to the City of Arvada and that the photo has not been improperly obtained.

Questions about the photo contest? Email [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#6e0b00090f090b2e0f1c180f0a0f40011c09).

## 31 Ways to Celebrate 31 Days of Park and Recreation Month in Arvada

With 220 sites over 4,200 acres of parkland, there are plenty of ways to celebrate. But in case you need some inspiration, here are 31 ways to celebrate 31 days of Parks and Recreation Month!

1. [1. McIlvoy Park - Arvada's oldest park](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_0)

![McIlvoy Park Pavilion](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=636)

The history of parks in Arvada dates back to 1919 when Mrs. Clemency McIlvoy deeded her home and the three acres that surround it to the Town of Arvada with the understanding that it would become our first park, now McIlvoy Park in Olde Town (5750 Upham Street). This was an early contribution to what has been sustained community support of outdoor spaces as cultural, recreational and civic centers.

1. [2. Majestic View Nature Center](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_1)

![Majestic View Nature Center](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=602)

The [Majestic View Nature Center](https://majesticviewnaturecenter.arvada.org/) is the City of Arvada’s environmental education facility, offering many school and group programs to engage kids with nature. Using the nature trails, wetland areas and prairie ecosystems to explore, we connect thousands of kids with Arvada’s parks to better understand nature.

1. [3. Visit One of Arvada's 100 Parks](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_2)

[![Park with a river and green grass and trees](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1832)](/508)

Small parks, big parks, dog parks, parks with community gardens, parks with BBQ grills, parks with trails. [Arvada's parks have it all](/508)! In fact, 96% of residents live within a 10-minute walk of a park, one of the highest rates of park access of any city our size in the country.

1. [4. 4th of July Fireworks](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_3)

[![Fourth of July Fireworks](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1337)](/494)

The City of Arvada is hosting its annual [4th of July fireworks display](/494) on Thursday, July 4, 2024 at Stenger Sports Complex (W 58th Avenue and Oak Street).

- Gates open to vehicles at 6:30 pm, Fireworks beginat approximately 9:15 p.m.
- Parking is free and is first-come, first-serve. Handicap parking available in the Stenger northeast lot.
- Food trucks will be onsite from approximately 5:30 to 9 pm.
- W. 58th Avenue will shut down to traffic beginning at 8 pm.
- No recreational vehicles (RVs), drones, alcohol, personal fireworks, charcoal grills, or pets allowed.
- Propane grills are allowed.

1. [5. Ralston Creek Trail](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_4)

![Ralston Creek trail sign next to a divided trail](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1836)

The [Ralston Creek Trail](/558) is Arvada's longest and most complete public trail, following the meandering creek and linking several City parks and open space areas. Along the way, you'll find many features that highlight Arvada's natural heritage: a rich variety of plant life, lakes and ponds, preserved wildlife habitats, bird sanctuaries, and historic sites.

1. [6. Sports Fields and Complexes](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_5)

![View of Stenger Sports Complex soccer fields](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1837)

Arvada is home to six athletic complexes that host a variety of organized sports activities, including soccer, lacrosse, rugby, baseball, and softball. The [City's athletic complexes](/649) include:

- Harold D. Lutz Sports Complex: 10664 W 58th Avenue
- Long Lake Regional Park: 17850 W 64th Avenue
- Stenger Sports Complex: 11200 W 58th Avenue
- Pioneer Park: 12100 W 82nd Avenue
- Foster Fields: 5300 Saulsbury Court
- Youth Memorial Sports Complex: 7619 Alkire Street

1. [7. Apex Recreation Facilities](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_6)

![Indoor pool facility ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1840)

Our partners at [Apex Park and Recreation District](https://apexprd.org/) offer more than a dozen high-quality recreation facilities, providing our community with an abundance of fitness and recreation opportunities. Celebrate Park and Recreation Month with Apex by playing bingo and get entered in a drawing to win a 20-visit punch card.

1. [8. West woods Golf Club](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_7)

![West Woods Golf Course ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1219)

Located in west Arvada, West Woods Golf Club features 27 unique championship golf holes. Each of our three nines provides brilliant natural scenery along with challenges for golfers of all skill levels. [Visit the West Woods Golf Club website](https://www.westwoodsgolf.com/) to book your tee time!

1. [9. Local Trails](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_8)

![Majestic View Trail ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1841)

[Arvada's 150-plus-mile trail network](/557) consists of Primary, Local and Regional Trails with both paved and soft surfaces. Trails are suitable for non-motorized recreational enjoyment as well as commuting. Our trail network includes [14 local trails](/560) that are shorter in length and are located in various parts throughout Arvada, often in neighborhoods and connected to parks.

1. [10. Skate Parks](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_9)

![Arvada Skate Park ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1842)

Located just east of the Apex Center, the [Arvada Skate Park](/643) is the third-largest park skate park in the country and has hosted several large-scale skating events. Arvada also is home to three skate spots located throughout the City: Memorial Park, Wolffe Park, and Skyline Park.

1. [11. Tennis Courts](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_10)

![Blue tennis courts with a city skyline in the background](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1843)

Tennis is a great way to be active and social while enjoying time outside. Arvada has 17 parks with tennis courts. Check out [our interactive courts map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=c750c8934aa44852bd149658e3aee3de) to see where they're all located!

1. [12. Movies around Town](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_11)

![Movie at a park at dusk ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1844)

[Arvada Festivals' Movies Around Town](https://arvadafestivals.com/movies-around-town) series is the perfect, free summer activity for the whole family. Celebrate Park and Recreation Month on Thursday, July 14 with a free showing of Top Gun: Maverick at Homestead Park!

1. [13. Van Bibber Creek Trail](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_12)

![Van Bibber Creek Trail](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=703)

The [Van Bibber Creek Trail](/558) is located within a peaceful stream corridor and winds through beautiful open space areas that offer a "back to nature" experience close to home. Creekside woodlands and meadows harbor many species of birds and other wildlife, particularly between Ward Road and Indiana Street.

Equestrians permitted from Ward Road to Indiana Street. Distance: 2.5 miles east of Indiana Street, 1 mile west of Easley Road.

1. [14. Outdoor Basketball](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_13)

![outdoor basketball court in a park](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1845)

Thirty of Arvada's parks feature basketball courts, including 17 full-courts and 14 half-courts.

1. [15. Fishing](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_14)

![A kid fishing at a reservoir ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1846)

Fishing is the perfect way to celebrate Park and Recreation Month in Arvada. [Fishing is permitted at most Arvada lakes or ponds](/654) unless otherwise posted. Some popular spots in the city include Jack B. Tomlinson Park, Lake Arbor, and Arvada-Blunn Reservoir.

1. [16. Little Dry Creek Trail](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_15)

![Little Dry Creek Trail](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=705)

[Little Dry Creek Trail](/558) stretches through rolling park and open space lands from Sheridan Boulevard west to Indiana Street. Far from dry, the creek supports many wetland areas with an abundance of wildlife at points along the trail. The best views are said to be found through Woodrun, Michael Northey, and Little Dry Creek Parks where you can enjoy picnic and play areas in these parks. The trail also runs through MacArthur and Lakecrest Parks.

1. [17. Olde Town Water Fountain](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_16)

![Olde Town Arvada Fountain ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1217)

[The Olde Town Water Fountain](/673) is the ideal summer activity. Before you visit, make sure you're aware of the daily hours of operation: 9 to 11 a.m., noon to 2 p.m., 4 to 6 p.m., and 8 to 10 p.m.

1. [18. Fitness Equipment](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_17)

![Outdoor fitness equipment ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1847)

Who needs the gym when you can work out at a park? Five Arvada parks have fitness equipment available to use, including Homestead, Lutz Overlook, Sarah George, Terrace, and Lake Arbor.

1. [19. Park and Recreation Professionals Day](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_18)

![Park maintenance worker riding a mower](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1848)

July 21 is National Park and Recreation Professionals Day! Our [parks maintenance team](/523) is made up of 55 skilled professionals who are dedicated to delivering superior services to enhance the lives of everyone in our community.

1. [20. Park Pavilions](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_19)

![park pavilion with tables and grills](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1849)

[Arvada's park pavilions](/518) are a great venue for gatherings, both large and small. The Arvada Parks Department offers 11 pavilions that can be reserved, along with 33 other pavilions that are first-come, first-serve.

1. [21. Ralston Central Splash Pad](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_20)

![Ralston Central Park and Splash Pad](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=945)

There's no better way to beat the July heat than the [Ralston Central Splash Pad](/675).

1. [22. Two Ponds National Wildlife Refuge](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_21)

![Two Ponds National Wildlife Refuge sign](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1850)

[Two Ponds National Wildlife Refuge](https://www.fws.gov/refuge/two-ponds) is a natural oasis with native wildlife and plants in an urban setting. It offers beautiful views of the Rocky Mountain Front Range with a network of trails meandering through prairie grasslands, woodlands, and wetlands. This 72-acre Refuge is managed to restore and preserve native prairie ecosystems, protect habitat for migratory and resident wildlife, and provide wildlife-dependent recreation opportunities for all ages.

1. [23. West Arvada Dog Park](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_22)

![West Arvada Dog Park ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1218)

The [West Arvada Dog Park](/529) is located at 17975 W. 64th Parkway in Arvada and is a "Special Use" park operated by volunteers on City-owned property. The park is funded 100% through donations.

1. [24. Lake Arbor Golf Course](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_23)

![Lake Arbor Golf Club ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1851)

[Lake Arbor Golf Club](https://www.lakearborgolf.com/) is a scenic 18-hole public course located at 8860 Wadsworth Blvd in east Arvada. The course features lush, medium-sized greens and narrow fairways. The classic layout is easily walked and provides picturesque views of the Rocky Mountains.

1. [25. Arvada-Blunn Reservoir](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_24)

![Two canoes on Arvada Blunn Reservoir ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1852)

The [Arvada-Blunn Reservoir](/658) is located in west Arvada, north of W. 66th Ave. and east of Highway 93, and is a scenic spot to fishing and boating.

1. [26. Open Space](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_25)

![Photo of a trail and open space in Arvada](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1215)

The Arvada Parks and [Open Space division](/514) maintains more than 3,200 acres of non-irrigated land throughout the City. Some popular Open Space areas to visit include Pattridge, Leyden Lake, Schaaf, Tucker Lake, and Van Bibber Creek.

1. [27. Bocce Ball and Horseshoes](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_26)

![horseshoes pit ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1855)

Looking for a fun, relaxing activity to do with friends and family? Take advantage of our horseshoe pits at Emil Schneider Park and Majestic View Park, or play some bocce ball at Sunrise Ridge Park.

1. [28. Little Raven Park](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_27)

![Little Raven Park ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1191)

[Little Raven Park](/868), located southeast of the Ward Rd. and W. 58th Ave. intersection, is Arvada's newest park. The idea to name the park in honor of Arapaho Chief Little Raven came from a nearby resident through a community engagement project. [Little Raven was known as a peacemaker](https://history.denverlibrary.org/colorado-biographies/chief-little-raven-c1810-1889) between native peoples of Colorado and white settlers in the 1800s.

1. [29. Equestrian facilities](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_28)

![Woman on a horse at the Arvada Outdoor Equestrian Center](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1835)

Arvada offers [extensive opportunities for the equestrian community](/641), including several equestrian use trails located throughout the community. Arvada is also home to an Indoor Equestrian Center, Outdoor Equestrian Center and the Horse Protection League.

1. [30. Disc Golf](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_29)

[![Man throwing a disc at disc golf course ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1222)](/640)

Arvada offers [two disc golf courses](/640), Johnny Roberts and Bird's Nest. Johnny Roberts is an 18-hole course located at Memorial Park, and Bird's Nest is a 27-hole course just east of Highway 93 on 64th Ave.

1. [31. Visit one of Arvada's 70 playgrounds](#tabf0e1dbac-369a-427e-ab20-d6dd7033965c_30)

![Oak Park Playground ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=1831)

With 70 playgrounds to explore in Arvada, you can't go wrong! Our playgrounds feature a variety of themes and equipment to entrain children of all ages, and are renovated yearly through the City's [Taking Lasting Care program](/860). Some popular favorites include Ralston Central, Memorial, Volunteer Firefighters, Rainbow East, Farmstead, and Lady Bug, among many, many others.
